steps.title: Welcome to ZaakAfhandelApp
steps.body: Let's take a quick spin through your case handling. We'll create a case together so you can see how the pieces fit. You'll add the record yourself.
Cases are the heart of the app: every task, document and decision hangs off a case. Open Cases from the menu to get started.
Add your first case: give it a case type and save. You can attach tasks, documents and decisions to it afterwards.
steps.task: Click New and save a case

steps.body: Tasks are the work items that move a case forward. Open Tasks from the menu.

steps.title: Where the automation lives
steps.body: Flows are what happens without anyone clicking. Read and edit them here.

steps.title: You're all set
steps.body: Nicely done. Your case handling has its first case. Head back to the Dashboard to watch it grow, and reopen this tour anytime from the … menu.

pages.title: Dashboard
pages._note: The six KPI cards live in `config.widgets[]` + `config.layout[]`, NOT in page-level `widgets[]`. CnPageRenderer renders a bare CnWidgetGrid for any page carrying body-slot page-level widgets and skips the typed page component entirely, so a `type:"dashboard"` page authored that way never mounts CnDashboardPage and silently loses its header, max-width, padding, sidebar and grid discipline (ConductionNL/hrmq#112). The v2 schema documents page-level `widgets[]` as preferred and calls `config.widgets` legacy — for a typed page that guidance is inverted, so please do not migrate these back.

config._note: CASE archetype — the operational heart of zaakgericht werken. ADR-062 rev3: the lead row splits the zaak into two field-scoped data widgets — 'Case identity' (identificatie/omschrijving/zaaktype/klant/verantwoordelijke org) and 'Process & planning' (archiefstatus/start-eind dates/uiterlijkeEinddatumAfdoening/betalingsindicatie) — 8-wide, with the KPI stats-block (open tasks/documents/decisions/roles, @objectId-scoped) and Related panel stacked 4-wide top-right. Below sit every child collection FK-scoped by zaak=@objectId: Tasks (taak.zaak), Documents (document.zaak), Decisions (besluit.zaak), Results (resultaat.zaak), Parties involved (rol.zaak), each keeping create ON (genuinely user-created children, pre-linked to this zaak) with viewAllRoute to its index, then a Files leaf. NOTE: zaak has NO OR 'status' field (status timeline is ZGW-API-only) so it is not shown as a column. The zaak schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes → no comms leaves; audit history stays in the sidebar tab only. ADR-049 Phase-4 (nextcloud-vue #89) sidebar work is PRESERVED from development: besluiten renders as a LIVE object-table sidebar tab off the parent-zaak-filtered ZGW endpoint, and six legacy component-stub tabs stay with their endpoint-reason _notes; statussen/berichten remain the hybrid ZGW-API data-source wish-list gap.

sidebarTabs._note: LIVE (ADR-049 Phase-4; nextcloud-vue #89 — CnObjectSidebar object-table tab widget): the ONE relation with a real parent-zaak-filtered endpoint — GET api/zrc/zaken/{zaakUuid}/besluiten (ZaakBesluitenController::index → {results:[{url,uuid,zaak,besluit}]}, zaakUuid=@objectId=the zaak OR id). CnObjectSidebar resolves widgets[].type:'object-table' to CnWidgetObjectTable and provides cnObjectContext {objectId,...}, so @objectId interpolates into the endpointSource.url PATH (useEndpointSource.interpolateUrlTokens); responsePath 'results' plucks the array. Columns mirror the zaakbesluit RELATION payload (besluit reference + relation url): the endpoint returns the relation, not the full besluit resource, so identificatie/besluittype/datum are NOT available here, and NO rowRoute is set — the relation payload carries no besluit id at row.id/@self.id and its 'besluit' field is a bare reference, so a row-click could not resolve a BesluitDetail target.

config._note: ACTION-ITEM archetype — a single work item that moves a case forward. A handler opens a taak to see what to do, by when, and against which case, so the body leads with the task fields (status, deadline, actie, toelichting) 8-wide next to a Related panel that resolves its FKs (parent zaak, klant, medewerker, contactmoment). A Files leaf holds any working attachments. Tasks have no child collections and the schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes, so the layout is deliberately compact — data + related + files, no comms leaves.

PERSON/ORGANISATION (relation) archetype — the 360 view of a citizen or company the municipality deals with. ADR-062 rev3: the lead row splits klant into 'Identity' (type/voornaam/achternaam/bsn/geboortedatum/bedrijfsnaam/kvkNummer) and 'Contact details' (emailadres/telefoonnummer/address/websiteUrl) 8-wide, with a KPI stats-block (cases/contact moments/tasks, klant=@objectId) and Related panel 4-wide top-right. Below: their Cases (zaak.klant), Contact moments (contactmoment.klant) and Tasks (taak.klant). Contact moments keep create ON (a new contact is naturally logged from the customer's page, pre-linked); Cases and Tasks are allowCreate:false — they are a 360 read/navigate view (a case starts from the case wizard, a task from its case). Although this is a person/organisation, the klant schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes, so NO comms leaves — emailadres/telefoonnummer stay plain fields.

config._note: EMPLOYEE (person) archetype — an internal handler's workload view. The medewerker schema is thin (voornaam/achternaam/email/telefoonnummer) and carries NO object FK fields, so the empty round-1 Related panel was dropped (honest content over padding). The lead row is the compact contact card 8-wide beside a KPI stats-block (assigned tasks + handled contact moments, medewerker=@objectId). The value of the page is the two workload lists below — Assigned tasks (taak.medewerker) and Contact moments handled (contactmoment.medewerker) — both allowCreate:false: this is a workload/assignment view, tasks and contacts are created against their case/customer, not from an employee profile. NO comms leaves: the schema declares no email/calendar/talk linkedTypes.

content.emptyText: No tasks assigned to this employee

config._note: INTERACTION-LOG archetype — a single logged contact (call, email, counter visit) captured against a klant/zaak. The record's whole value is the note plus who/when/which-channel, so the body is a wide 3-column data widget (notitie, kanaal, startDate, status) with a Related panel that resolves its FKs (klant, zaak, taak, medewerker) so the handler can jump to the case or customer. No child collections; the contactmoment schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes (the channel/date are plain fields), so no comms leaves — the layout is intentionally minimal: data + related.

MESSAGE/CORRESPONDENCE archetype — a single message (onderwerp + berichttekst/inhoud) exchanged with a customer, with a bijlage attachment type. ADR-062 rev3: the round-1 Related panel was dropped — bericht carries NO object FK (no zaak/klant), so it had nothing to resolve. The lead row is now a field-scoped data widget (onderwerp/berichttekst/berichtType/dates/soortGebruiker/bijlageType, IDs hidden) 8-wide beside a Files leaf 4-wide for the actual attachment surface (bijlageType indicates enclosures). The bericht schema declares NO email/calendar/talk linkedTypes — stored data, not a live mailbox — so no email leaf.

ROLE / PARTY-IN-CASE archetype — a junction record binding a betrokkene (person/organisation) to a zaak in a specific capacity (initiator, behandelaar, belanghebbende…). The body is data-led (roltype, omschrijvingGeneriek, betrokkeneType, contactpersoonRol, roltoelichting) 8-wide beside a Related panel that resolves the linked zaak and the betrokkene so a handler can navigate both sides of the relationship. It has no child collections and the schema declares NO comms linkedTypes, so the layout is deliberately minimal: data + related, no files or comms leaves.

CATALOG/TEMPLATE (config) archetype — the definition of a case type (doel, aanleiding, doorlooptijd, servicenorm, publication settings, validity dates). This is a configuration record with many attributes, so the body uses a wide 3-column data widget to show the full definition, with a KPI stats-block (cases-of-this-type count, zaaktype=@objectId) and Related panel stacked top-right, and — the key operational payoff — an object-list of Cases created from this type (zaak.zaaktype=@objectId, allowCreate:false: a computed/navigate view, cases start from the case wizard). NO comms/files leaves: a zaaktype is a template, it doesn't communicate or carry attachments.

content.emptyText: No cases created from this type yet

config._note: DECISION-DOCUMENT archetype — the formal besluit that (often) closes a case. The schema is thin (besluit, url, zaak), so the compact data card sits beside a Related panel that resolves the parent zaak, and the page gives prominence to the Files leaf: a besluit is a legal document and its attachment/PDF is the artefact people come to read. NO comms leaves (a decision doesn't hold a mailbox) — the document itself is the focus, so Files spans full width below the header row.

DOCUMENT archetype — a ZGW enkelvoudig informatieobject. The whole point of the page is the file plus its rich records-management metadata, so the layout is document-first: the Files leaf takes a prominent 8-wide column (open/preview the actual content), with the metadata data widget (titel, auteur, status, vertrouwelijkheidaanduiding, versie, ondertekening, integriteit, informatieobjecttype) 4-wide beside it, and a Related panel resolving the parent zaak below. NO comms leaves — a document is an artefact, not a conversation.

OUTCOME archetype — the resultaat classifies how a case ended (resultaattype + toelichting) and feeds the archiving/selectielijst regime. The schema is intentionally thin, so the page is deliberately minimal: a data widget (resultaattype, toelichting) beside a Related panel that resolves the parent zaak. No child collections, no attachments to speak of, and NO comms linkedTypes — a result is a classification, so data + related is the right, honest layout rather than padding it with empty leaves.

STATUS-EVENT archetype — a single entry in a case's status timeline (statustype, datum, statustoelichting). It is one immutable point in the zaak's history, so the page is intentionally minimal: a data widget showing the status entry beside a Related panel that resolves the parent zaak so the reader can jump back to the full timeline on the case. No children, no attachments, NO comms linkedTypes — padding a single timeline event with leaves would be dishonest, so data + related is exactly right.

pages._note: ADR-112 / ADR-114 Decision 3. Nothing is invented: the audit trail already existed and was an entry in the SETTINGS foldout, which is where configuration belongs (ADR-044 Decision 3) and an audit trail is not configuration — it is a reading of what happened. The page is untouched and stays routable at /auditTrail; only its menu entry moves, because a report is a card or an entry, never both (ADR-112 Decision 2).

pages.title: Flows
pages._note: ADR-110 Decision 4. type:"index" over the NAMED flows source, which is the canonical shape: a flow lives in OpenRegister's native flow store, not a register/schema pair, so the object-backed index cannot address it, and nextcloud-vue marks the dedicated `flows` page type deprecated. rowRoute names FlowDetail by route NAME, without which the row click and the Edit action fall back to the source's own /flows path rather than the page declared here.
